summary: North Macedonia’s commitments combine conservation, cross-sector mitigation and agricultural action, but they do not specify ecosystem-restoration or protected-area targets. For conservation, projected carbon sinks in 2030 are assumed to be 7% higher than in 2014, while LULUCF removals are targeted to increase by 95%. These ambitions are relevant to a landscape comprising 48.7% forest, 11.8% grassland and 35.3% agriculture, although no affected areas or baselines are provided for the removal targets. Under the cross-sector “Both” commitment, North Macedonia lists 63 mitigation policies and measures spanning energy, agriculture, LULUCF and waste, along with enabling measures. For agriculture, a 29% reduction is reported without specifying the baseline, activity or implementation period. Overall, the numerical commitments concern percentage changes and a policy count rather than land or ecosystem coverage.

targets.context: No land-area coverage is specified; forest currently covers 48.7% of the country.
The measures span energy, agriculture, LULUCF, waste and enabling sectors.
The baseline and covered area are unspecified; agriculture covers 35.3% of the country.
No affected area is specified; forest covers 12,409 km² and grassland 3,000 km².
